sections.content:
You know *pase lo que pase*, *diga lo que diga*, *venga quien venga* and *quieras o no* from B2 Unit 8, and *sea cual sea* from B2 Unit 14. The same verb is said twice, around a relative word, to say that it makes no difference. New here are *cueste lo que cueste* ("whatever it takes") and the past version.

For the past, put both verbs in the imperfect subjunctive (B1 Unit 4): *Costara lo que costara, estaban decididos a ganar.* "Whatever it cost, they were determined to win." The two verbs always match in person and tense.

The *o no* pattern can also repeat the verb: *quieras o no quieras*, *quiera o no quiera*. *Quieras o no* is the short form.

items.spanish: Cueste lo que cueste, terminaremos el trabajo.
items.english: Whatever it takes, we will finish the work.

items.spanish: Pase lo que pase, te voy a apoyar.
items.english: Come what may, I am going to support you.

items.spanish: Costara lo que costara, estaban decididos a ganar.
items.english: Whatever it cost, they were determined to win.

items.spanish: Quieras o no, tienes que ir.
items.english: Whether you like it or not, you have to go.

sections.content: Both verbs must be in the subjunctive and must match: *cueste lo que cueste*, never *cueste lo que cuesta*. In a story, switch both to the imperfect: *costara lo que costara*.
